title: Wangxian: Forgetting Envy 3
content:
The day after crossing paths with Luo Qingyang and her husband, the pair arrived in a sleepy riverside town in Guangling.

Wei Wuxian shielded his brow against the glare, spotting a fluttering tavern banner just up the road. "Let's take a breather over there."

Lan Wangji nodded, and they fell into step side by side.

Ever since that chaotic night at the Guanyin Temple in Yunmeng, Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji had been drifting along together, taking Little Apple on a lazy tour across the realm. True to form, Lan Wangji still went wherever chaos called; whenever whispers reached them of restless spirits harassing local villagers, they'd swing by, take care of it without breaking a sweat, and spend the rest of the time sightseeing and savoring the local flavor. For three months, they had completely tuned out the cultivation world, living a life of utter, carefree indulgence.

Stepping into the tavern, they slipped into an out-of-the-way corner table. When the waiter bustled over, he couldn't help stealing a few glances at their striking demeanor. His eyes darted from the pristine sword at Lan Wangji's hip to the black flute tucked into Wei Wuxian's sash, and his mind immediately linked them to a certain pair dominating the rumor mills lately. But after squinting discreetly for a good while, he noted the white-robed gentleman was noticeably lacking the signature forehead ribbon of the Gusu Lan Clan, so he didn't dare assume.

Wei Wuxian called for wine, while Lan Wangji ordered a handful of dishes. Listening to that deep, measured voice rattle off the names, Wei Wuxian propped his chin on one hand, while his other hand lounged beneath the table, idly wrapping a ribbon of snow-white silk around his fingers. A playful smirk tugged at his lips. Once the waiter scurried off, he teased, "Ordering that many spicy dishes—are you actually going to eat them, or just stare at them?"

Lan Wangji picked up his teacup, took a neat sip, and remarked coolly, "Sit properly."

Wei Wuxian tilted his head. "Your cup's empty."

Lan Wangji went still for a second. He refilled the cup, lifted it back to his lips, and after a moment's pause, tried again: "...Sit properly."

"What's wrong with how I'm sitting?" Wei Wuxian whined with mock offense. "It's not like I propped my legs on the tabletop like back in the day."

Lan Wangji showed immense restraint before managing, "Then do not rest them elsewhere, either."

Wei Wuxian gave him a wide-eyed, innocent blink. "Where else am I putting them?"

Lan Wangji said nothing, his gaze heavy.

"Second Young Master Lan sure has a lot of rules," Wei Wuxian hummed, amused. "Why don't you teach me how to sit, then?"

Lan Wangji set his cup down, swept his gaze over him, and gave his sleeve a firm shake, looking entirely ready to stand up and teach him a thorough lesson—right until a burst of raucous laughter exploded from the center of the room.

A man at a neighboring table was practically crowing with schadenfreude. "I called it! I knew Jin Guangyao's tricks would catch up with him sooner or later! I've been waiting for this day forever, and it finally blew up in his face! Good and evil get their due in the end, justice never misses!"

Hearing that kind of self-righteous screeching gave Wei Wuxian an odd, nostalgic twinge; the phrasing and righteous venom were all too familiar, just swapped onto a new target. He leaned in slightly, ears perking up.

A rogue cultivator gestured grandly with a pair of chopsticks, playing the enlightened critic. "The ancients had it right! The fancier these high-and-mighty hypocrites look on the outside, the filthier their dirty laundry is behind closed doors!"

"Damn right! Not a single decent bone among them. All those fancy titles and upright gentleman acts—just cheap masks to fool the common rabble."

Another patron washed down a mouthful of meat with a heavy swig of wine, spraying flecks of grease as he ran his mouth. "Speaking of which, that Sisi woman used to be the hottest courtesan around, but she’s aged so terribly I didn't even recognize her. Absolute mood killer! Though to be fair, Jin Guangshan died a pretty gruesome death himself, ahahaha!"

"Leave it to Jin Guangyao to cook up a sick stunt like that for his own father! Fitting, really. Absolutely poetic!"

"What boggles my mind is why Jin Guangyao didn't just slit her throat. When it comes to witnesses, you eliminate them! Was he an idiot, or what?"

"Who says he was an idiot? He's Jin Guangshan's seed after all, probably cut from the same lecherous cloth. Who knows, maybe he had peculiar tastes and kept Sisi around for some... illicit, behind-closed-doors fun, eh?"

"Heh, I had the same thought! But haven't you heard the gossip? Word is, sleeping with his own half-sister gave him such a fright that he developed a certain... private dysfunction. Even if the spirit was willing, the flesh was useless, hahahaha!"

Listening to this unhinged barrage of slander and creative fanfiction, Wei Wuxian felt right at home. It reminded him of the rumors claiming he’d abducted a thousand virgins to the Burial Mounds for depraved demonic rituals. The absurdity was almost endearing. He thought to himself: Well, at least my rumors sounded a little cooler than whatever they're cooking up for Jin Guangyao.

As the banter grew increasingly vulgar, Lan Wangji’s brows knit into a tight furrow. Thankfully, someone with a shred of sense at their table couldn't stomach it anymore and muttered, "Keep it down, will you? Not exactly polite dinner talk."

The loudmouths sneered, entirely unbothered. "What're you sweating about? Nobody knows us here."

"Exactly! And so what if someone hears? Since when does the law police table talk?"

"You think the Lanling Jin Clan still runs the show like they used to? Think they can muzzle everyone? Let them try throwing their weight around now! If people don't like hearing it, they can lump it!"

Another cultivator waved a hand to steer the topic away. "Alright, alright, give it a rest. Eat your food. Doesn't matter what kind of storm Jin Guangyao kicked up while he was alive; now he's just stuck in a pine box throwing hands with Nie Mingjue."

"Doubt he's throwing hands—it's more like Nie Mingjue is snapping his bones into toothpicks by now."

"Tell me about it! I went to the sealing ceremony, and the resentful energy rolling off that sarcophagus was so foul not a single blade of grass survived within a mile! I genuinely wonder if that box can actually hold them for a century."

"Whether it holds or not isn't your headache to nurse," someone snorted. "That mess belongs to the great sects. Either way, Lanling Jin is finished. The sky's fallen on them for good."

"Though, during the ceremony, Zewu-jun looked awful."

"How could he not? The coffin holds both his sworn brothers, and his clan's younger generation spends their days running wild with a fierce corpse, relying on a walking dead man to bail them out on night-hunts! No wonder he went straight into secluded meditation. If Lan Wangji doesn't drag himself home soon, Lan Qiren is going to blow a gasket in public..."

Lan Wangji took a quiet breath, completely deadpan.

Wei Wuxian smothered a snort into his sleeve.

The gossip table kept rolling: "Speaking of which, that sealing ceremony actually caught me off guard. Who would've thought Nie Huaisang had it in him? When he volunteered to take charge, I was convinced he'd botch it completely. The guy's famous for playing dumb."

"Right?! And out of nowhere, he runs the whole ritual just as smoothly as Lan Qiren could have."

Listening to their collective awe, Wei Wuxian smirked inwardly. You haven't seen anything yet. Give it a few decades—the seemingly clueless leader of the Qinghe Nie Sect might just show his fangs and shock the cultivation world a few dozen times more.

The waiter finally returned, setting down steaming bowls alongside a jug of wine. Wei Wuxian filled his cup to the brim and took a slow, leisurely sip.

Suddenly, a clear, youthful voice cut through the hum of the dining hall: "Is the Yin Tiger Tally really inside that coffin?"

The room fell into an abrupt, uneasy hush.

After a beat, someone chimed in, "Who knows? Probably. If Jin Guangyao didn't keep it on him, where else would he tuck it away?"

"Hard to say, though. Didn't they say the tally is just scrap metal now? Completely drained of power."

The young cultivator sat alone at a nearby table, cradling a sheathed sword against his chest. His eyes gleamed with raw ambition. "Is that coffin really that indestructible? What if someone wanted to crack it open and check for the tally?"

Someone scoffed loudly from across the floor. "Who'd have the guts?!"

"Qinghe Nie, Gusu Lan, and Yunmeng Jiang all stationed disciples around the burial grounds. Who's suicidal enough to try?"

Murmurs of agreement rippled through the tavern. The young man didn't press the matter, lifting his tea bowl to take a drink as if dropping the thought entirely. But the look in his eyes never wavered.

Wei Wuxian had seen that exact gleam in countless eyes before. And he knew with absolute certainty that this wouldn't be the last time he'd see it.

Once they finished, they took their leave. Wei Wuxian hopped back onto Little Apple's back, letting Lan Wangji lead the donkey by the reins ahead of him.

Swaying with the beast’s lazy trot, Wei Wuxian slipped the dark flute from his belt and brought it to his lips. A clean, airy melody soared like a wild bird into the sky.

Lan Wangji’s boots slowed to a halt, listening in quiet reverence.

It was the very song he had sung in the depths of the Xuanwu cave while they were trapped in the dark.

The very song Wei Wuxian had instinctively whistled at Mount Dafan upon his return—the melody that had betrayed his identity in a single breath.

As the final note faded into the breeze, Wei Wuxian gave him a playful wink. "Well? How was that? Sound good?"

Lan Wangji nodded softly. "A rare treat."

Wei Wuxian caught the jab—rare meaning it was a miracle his terrible memory had actually held onto the tune. He laughed aloud. "Hey, don't hold a grudge over that! I was wrong before, alright? Besides, you can't blame me for having a sieve for a brain. Blame my mother."

Lan Wangji glanced back. "Why?"

Propping an elbow on the donkey's head, Wei Wuxian twirled Chenqing with a practiced flick of his fingers. "My mother used to say: remember the kindness others show you, and forget the favors you do for others. Don't weigh your heart down with useless clutter, and you'll always live happy and free."

It was one of the precious few memories of his parents that had managed to stick through the years.

His thoughts drifted for a fleeting second before snapping back. Seeing Lan Wangji gazing up at him with unblinking focus, Wei Wuxian added with a grin, "My mother also said..."

Lan Wangji waited, and when the rest didn't follow, prompted, "Said what?"

Wei Wuxian curled an index finger, his face deadpan and serious. Lan Wangji stepped closer. Wei Wuxian leaned down, murmuring right into his ear: "...She said you belong to me now."

Lan Wangji’s brow twitched. Before he could part his lips, Wei Wuxian cut him off in a breathless rush: "Shameless, improper, frivolous, ridiculous, spouting nonsense again—right? There, said it for you! It's always those exact same words, you haven't changed a bit. But hey, I belong to you too, so we're even. Fair?"

When it came to verbal sparring, Lan Wangji was never a match for him. He simply murmured, "If you say so."

Wei Wuxian gave the reins a tug. "All jokes aside, I threw over eighty titles at you for this tune. Not a single one hit the mark?"

"None," Lan Wangji answered firmly.

Wei Wuxian pouted. "How picky! I thought 'The Ballad of Lan Zhan and Wei Ying's Undying Devotion' was a stroke of genius."

Lan Wangji said nothing.

"Or 'The Hanguang-Yiling Everyday Melody'!" Wei Wuxian rambled on. "Has a nice ring to it, really tells a story..."

As if desperately cutting off any further artistic atrocities, Lan Wangji broke in, "It has one."

Wei Wuxian blinked. "Has what?"

"A name."

Wei Wuxian gasped in mock outrage. "It had a name this whole time?! Why didn't you speak up sooner? What is it? You kept me in the dark while I burned through all those brain cells trying to come up with one!"

Lan Wangji paused for a beat.

"Wangxian."

Wei Wuxian stared. "Huh?"

"The song," Lan Wangji murmured, steady and quiet. "It is called Wangxian."

Wei Wuxian’s eyes blew wide.

A second later, he threw his head back, clutching his ribs as laughter bubbled out of him. "Hahaha! No wonder you kept your mouth shut! Sneaking our names together like that—your intentions couldn't be more obvious! Not bad, Lan Zhan! When on earth did you come up with that, hahah!"

Lan Wangji seemed to have anticipated the reaction. Watching him rock back and forth on the donkey’s back, he could only give a subtle, helpless shake of his head. His expression was the picture of patient resignation, but the corners of his lips had already curled into an impossibly soft, quiet smile, his pale eyes rippling with warmth.

He reached up, bracing a steady hand against Wei Wuxian’s waist to keep him from tumbling into the grass.

Once he finally caught his breath, Wei Wuxian cleared his throat, nodding with absolute solemnity. "Wangxian. It's good. It’s perfect! I love it. Honestly, it couldn't be called anything else."

Lan Wangji kept his face impassive. "I like it as well."

"Sounds remarkably dignified, very Gusu Lan," Wei Wuxian declared. "I say you should slap it right into your clan's official music compendium and make every disciple learn it by heart. And if they dare ask, 'Hanguang-jun, what does the title mean?' you can look them dead in the eye and tell them the whole sordid story of how it came to be."

Tuning out the shameless chatter, Lan Wangji gripped Little Apple's lead firmly in his hand and continued down the winding road.

Wei Wuxian’s mouth didn't stop moving for a second: "Where to next? It's been ages since I’ve had Emperor's Smile—how about we swing by Gusu and hit Caiyi Town first?"

"Alright."

"After all these years, they must have cleared out that Waterborne Abyss by now, right? If your uncle can tolerate looking at me, you can hide me away in your Jingshi with a few jars of wine. If he can't stand the sight of my face, we can go track down Wen Ning instead. Sounds like he and Sizhui are having a blast on their night-hunts."

"Mn."

"Though I heard the Lan Clan just dropped an updated edition of the sect rules? Tell me, is there even enough room left on that discipline wall of yours to carve them all in..."

A gentle breeze swept across the meadows, rustling their robes like ripples across a springtime lake.

Gazing at the broad, white-robed back walking ahead of him, Wei Wuxian squinted into the wind, crossed his legs over the saddle, and was mildly amazed to find he could maintain this bizarre posture without losing his balance.

It was the most mundane, silly little realization, yet he felt an urgent, childish need to show it off right away.

He called out with a bright laugh: "Lan Zhan! Look at me! Quick, look at me!"

Just like all those years ago, Wei Wuxian called out to him with a smile, and Lan Wangji turned to look.

And from that moment on, he could never look away again.
